definitions.definition: For x∈ℝⁿ and r>0, e(x,r)=‖u_t(x,r)‖₂²+∑_{j=1}^n‖∂_{x_j}u(x,r)‖₂²; the vector norms are Euclidean, and the spatial-gradient term is the Frobenius/Hilbert–Schmidt square of the Jacobian.

definitions.type: For smooth u:ℝⁿ×(0,∞)→ℝᵐ, a differential operator with Δ_xu:ℝⁿ×(0,∞)→ℝᵐ.
definitions.definition: For each (x,r), (Δ_xu)(x,r)=∑_{j=1}^n ∂²u(x,r)/∂x_j², with each second derivative taken componentwise in ℝᵐ.

definitions.type: positive integer k maps to Euclidean/Borel/Lebesgue measure space on ℝᵏ
definitions.definition: For each positive integer k, identify ℝᵏ with the finite product Fin k→ℝ, equip it with its Euclidean norm and topology, the Borel σ-algebra generated by that topology, and product Lebesgue measure (the product of one-dimensional Lebesgue volume on each coordinate).

inputs.statement: For every t>0, e(·,t) is Lebesgue integrable. For every t>0 there exist a finite closed interval J=[s₀,s₁]⊂(0,∞) with s₀<t<s₁ and a compact set C⊂ℝⁿ such that, for every s∈J and x∉C, u(x,s)=q, ∂_s u(x,s)=0, and ∂_{x_j}u(x,s)=0 for every j∈Fin n; for every s∈J, the maps x↦u_t(x,s), x↦∂_{x_j}u(x,s), x↦e(x,s), and x↦e_t(x,s) are continuous on ℝⁿ and vanish for every x∉C, for each j∈Fin n. The ambient measurable space on ℝⁿ is the Borel σ-algebra generated by its Euclidean topology, and Lebesgue measure μ satisfies μ(K)<∞ for every compact K⊂ℝⁿ.

For every t>0, e(·,t) is Lebesgue integrable. For every t>0 there exist a finite closed interval J=[s₀,s₁]⊂(0,∞) with s₀<t<s₁ and a compact set C⊂ℝⁿ such that, for every s∈J and x∉C, u(x,s)=q, ∂_s u(x,s)=0, and ∂_{x_j}u(x,s)=0 for every j∈Fin n; for every s∈J, the maps x↦u_t(x,s), x↦∂_{x_j}u(x,s), x↦e(x,s), and x↦e_t(x,s) are continuous on ℝⁿ and vanish for every x∉C, for each j∈Fin n. The ambient measurable space on ℝⁿ is the Borel σ-algebra generated by its Euclidean topology, and every compact K⊂ℝⁿ is Borel measurable with finite Lebesgue measure μ(K)<∞.
For measurable topological X with measurable opens, normed additive commutative V, measure μ finite on compacts and continuous compactly supported f:X→V, f is integrable.

Let X be a finite-dimensional real normed additive group with Borel measurable space and an additive Haar measure μ. Let F,G,W be real normed additive groups and B:F→L(G,W) a continuous bilinear map. For f:X→F, f′:X→L(X,F), g:X→G, g′:X→L(X,G) and v∈X, if x↦B(f′(x)v,g(x)), x↦B(f(x),g′(x)v), and x↦B(f(x),g(x)) are μ-integrable; f has Frechet derivative f′ on tsupport(g); and g has Frechet derivative g′ on tsupport(f), then ∫B(f(x),g′(x)v)dμ=−∫B(f′(x)v,g(x))dμ.

hypotheses: E has a measurable space, Borel space, finite-dimensional real normed additive structure; μ is an additive Haar measure.
F,G,W have real normed additive structures and B is continuous bilinear.
The three displayed scalar/product functions are μ-integrable.
At every x in tsupport(g), f has Frechet derivative f′(x); at every x in tsupport(f), g has Frechet derivative g′(x).

inputs.statement: For every finite index type ι, the product Lebesgue volume measure on ι→ℝ is an additive Haar measure.

locals.declaration: Fix an arbitrary spatial coordinate index j∈Fin n for the integration-by-parts calculation; the resulting identity is then summed over all j.

locals.type: the jth standard basis vector of ℝⁿ
locals.declaration: Let v_j be the jth standard basis vector in ℝⁿ.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary r>0 and spatial index j∈Fin n; define v_j=e_j, f_j(x)=∂_{x_j}u(x,r), and g(x)=u_t(x,r). N001 directly supplies a closed time window containing r and a compact C outside which u=q throughout that window. Because u is jointly smooth and is constant on the open set (ℝⁿ\\C)×J, f_j,g and their Frechet derivatives vanish outside C and are continuous. Thus the three functions ⟨Df_j(x)[v_j],g(x)⟩, ⟨f_j(x),Dg(x)[v_j]⟩, and ⟨f_j(x),g(x)⟩ are continuous and supported in C. By M001 and the ambient facts exported in N001, all three are integrable. Smoothness gives the Frechet derivative identities everywhere, in particular on tsupport(g) for f_j and tsupport(f_j) for g. Apply M011 with X=ℝⁿ, F=G=ℝᵐ, W=ℝ, B the Euclidean dot product and direction v_j. It gives ∫⟨∂_{x_j}u,∂_{x_j}u_t⟩=−∫⟨∂_{x_jx_j}u,u_t⟩. Joint smoothness also gives the mixed-partial identity ∂_t∂_{x_j}u=∂_{x_j}u_t used in differentiating the gradient square. Since j was arbitrary, sum these identities over j=1,…,n. The finite-dimensional product rule yields ∫e_t=2∫u_t·(u_{tt}−Δ_xu). N002 identifies E′(r)=∫e_t, proving the desired energy-derivative formula for arbitrary r>0.

applications.bindings: X=ℝⁿ with Borel measurable space and Lebesgue measure, V=ℝ, f equal successively to each of the three scalar product functions formed from u_t, ∂_{x_j}u, and their spatial Frechet derivatives.
